historical_record.description: The Board of Permit Appeals overruled the Department of Public Works and granted the permit to alter the building at 1362 Post Street, with conditions.

Redevelopment Agency inspectors recorded ten apartments. The exterior was in good condition and the interior fair. The street front was rated of notable visual merit. Assessed at $3,040 for the land and $7,100 for the improvements.
The Redevelopment Agency agreed to sell the building to the Multi-Services Center for Koreans, a nonprofit, which was to buy and rehabilitate it.

In the Redevelopment Agency's 1962 acquisition appraisal for Western Addition A-2, the appraiser Maury Holmes put the market value of the property at $55,000 and rated it in fair condition. He described a two-and-a-half-story frame building with eleven apartments, from two to four rooms, each with its own bath and kitchen.
